subject: Request: Executive clearance for Pinnacle Private deployment variance
messages:
From: Aisha Verma <a.verma@pinnaclehealth.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@pinnaclehealth.com>, Pinnacle Procurement <procure@pinnaclehealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T08:47:00-08:00
Subject: Private deployment - special hosting & audit requests

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Pinnacle’s engineering and security teams are aligned on moving forward with a Private deployment (VPC). Before we sign, our legal and compliance leads have three non-standard requests that must be captured in the contract: 

1) Audit window: we need quarterly on-site audit rights with a 30–45 day notification window and a 5-business-day window where we can request a live inspection.
2) Data egress constraints: data must remain in our US-only tenant and outbound egress to third-party processing is prohibited without prior written consent.
3) Hardware controls: customer-managed KMS/HSM integration + a list of approved HSM models; we will require attestations on key handling.

We realize these are uncommon. Procurement has attached redlines and an audit schedule for your deal desk to review. Can you escalate to your execs for clearance on the audit cadence and the HSM ask? We can be flexible on timing if Redwood needs a limited carveout.

Attached: pinnacle_redlines_v2.pdf, audit-window-proposal.xlsx

Best,
Aisha Verma
Head of Security Compliance
Pinnacle Health

[Attachment: pinnacle_redlines_v2.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: audit-window-proposal.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com

Date: 2026-11-18T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment - special hosting & audit requests

Aisha — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. I’ve looped in Lauren (Legal) and Rishi (Deal Desk / Security liaison). We’ll review the redlines and escalate any asks that need exec approval. A couple quick clarifying questions up front: 

- Is the 5-business-day live inspection an additional slot on top of quarterly audits, or part of the quarterly process?
- For HSMs: can you share the minimum FIPS/PCI/CC level you require? If you already listed models in the redline, point me to the page number and I’ll surface that to infra.

I’ll follow up once we have internal guidance.

—Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Aisha Verma <a.verma@pinnaclehealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Private deployment - special hosting & audit requests

Forwarding Pinnacle’s asks. Quick read: audit cadence + live inspection window + customer-managed HSM + strict egress block. Highlights for execs:

- The audit cadence (quarterly with short-notice live inspections) increases operational exposure and will require a scoped on-prem checklist and an SLA for inspection turnaround.
- Customer-managed HSM is feasible technically but requires an exception to our standard managed-key model; legal needs to define indemnity and support boundaries.
- Egress prohibition is the most material: it affects our fallback routing and some cross-region disaster recovery plans; we need an explicit carveout or a routing policy that allows emergency egress under defined approvals.

Action request: we need exec sign-off on a) limited audit exposure (define max on-site days per year), b) one-time exception for customer-managed HSM with acceptance of an engineering support SLA, and c) clear language around emergency egress approvals. Please elevate to Sarah (CRO) + Mark (CPO) — I’ve drafted suggested language below.

Draft suggestion (for deal desk):
- Audit: Redwood will allow quarterly audits with a maximum of two live on-site inspection days per year; live inspections require 5 business days’ notice and are subject to Redwood-provided escort and limited scope.
- HSM: Customer-managed HSM allowed with a validated model list; Redwood provides integration support limited to key exchange and attestation; all key custody remains customer responsibility.
- Egress: Data will remain in-customer-tenant and region; emergency egress allowed only with written approval from Redwood’s Chief Product Officer and Security Lead.

I recommend execs approve with the above constraints to keep deal economics intact.

—Lauren Bishop
Sr. Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: deployment-architecture-diagram.png (png)]

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: Sarah Collins <sarah.collins@redwood.com>, Mark Rivera <mark.rivera@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T13:02:00-08:00
Subject: Exec escalation: Pinnacle Health — approval request (deal desk)

Team — escalating for quick exec guidance. Summary: Pinnacle requires quarterly audits + short-notice live inspection window (5 business days), customer-managed HSM, and strict egress prohibition. Commercial ask includes a 25% one-time platform discount tied to a 3-year commitment (HubSpot: HSP-12458 / DEAL-2026-1198).

Risk vs. mitigation (short):
- Audit: operational burden; mitigate by limiting live on-site inspection days to two/year and requiring scoped checklists.
- HSM: increases support complexity; mitigate by limiting supported HSM models and requiring customer-managed KMS integration testing before cutover.
- Egress ban: impacts disaster recovery and fallback; mitigate by requiring emergency egress approval process and a signed MOU for DR scenarios.

Requested exec decisions:
1) Approve limited audit exposure (two live days/year, 5-business-day notice).
2) Allow customer-managed HSM with the limited model list and support SLA.
3) Accept egress prohibition only if emergency egress policy and DR MOU are included.
4) Approve up to 20% one-time discount (counter to Procurement’s 25%) and authorize Deal Desk to finalize.

Please reply-all with sign-off or objections within 24 hours so we can keep the November close.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Manager, Deal Desk | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: none]

From: Mark Rivera <mark.rivera@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: Sarah Collins <sarah.collins@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T16:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Exec escalation: Pinnacle Health — approval request (deal desk)

Approved with conditions — Mark Rivera (CPO)

I agree with the mitigations Rishi proposed. Approve the following:
- Audit: allow quarterly audits with a hard cap of two live on-site inspection days per 12-month period, 5-business-day notice required, Redwood escort and predefined scope only.
- HSM: allow customer-managed HSM but require Redwood-approved model list and a pre-production integration test; engineering support limited to specific integration steps; customer signs an addendum limiting Redwood liability for key custody.
- Egress: accept egress prohibition with the explicit caveat that emergency egress for disaster recovery requires written approval from CPO + Security Lead and must be documented in a DR MOU.
- Commercial: approve up to 20% one-time platform discount contingent on a signed 3-year commitment and prepayment of year 1.

Sarah, please confirm the Security Lead sign-off offline; once we have that, Rishi: proceed to finalize and capture redline language.

—Mark
Chief Product Officer | Redwood Inference

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
To: Aisha Verma <a.verma@pinnaclehealth.com>, Pinnacle Procurement <procure@pinnaclehealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-19T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Final: Pinnacle Private deployment — executive decisions and next steps

Hi Aisha / Tom,

Thanks for your patience — our execs have reviewed your requests and we have conditional approval to proceed. Summary of what Redwood will accept (to be captured in the SOW and addendum):

1) Audit: Redwood will permit quarterly audits. Live on-site inspections are capped at two days per 12-month period and require 5 business days’ notice. Redwood will provide an escort and a scoped checklist; inspections will be limited to infrastructure relevant to Pinnacle’s environment.

2) HSM: Customer-managed HSM is allowed. We require the integration to be validated via a pre-production test and that the HSM model be on Redwood’s approved list. Key custody remains customer responsibility; Redwood will provide limited integration support. An addendum will limit Redwood’s liability for key management.

3) Egress: Data will remain in your US tenant. Emergency egress for DR is permitted only with written approval from Redwood’s CPO and Security Lead and must be documented in a DR MOU.

4) Commercial: Redwood can offer a one-time 20% platform discount tied to a signed 3-year agreement and prepayment of year one.

Next steps:
- Rishi will send redline language for the addendum and updated SOW (HubSpot: HSP-12458).
- Legal (Lauren) will prepare the HSM addendum and DR MOU template.
- Engineering to schedule pre-prod HSM integration test (please provide preferred HSM model list).

If any of these conditions are a dealbreaker, let us know immediately. Otherwise we’ll circulate the redlines by end of week for signature.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
